letters.desc: Buckeye supports applying cost protection rules to large load interconnections already in the study queue, not just future filings, because transmission investment to serve those loads is already underway and creating cost-shift risk today.
quotes: Buckeye supports a transition mechanism for the treatment of large load interconnections that are already being studied.

letters.org: Industrial Energy Consumers of America et al.
letters.desc: The filers ask FERC to establish a transition period with an effective date no earlier than 2027, and to exempt in-progress manufacturing projects with pending studies, transactions, or demonstrated site control from any new mandatory federal interconnection rule.
quotes: the new rule should not apply to new large loads where the customers have pending transactions, pending studies, pending new customer service applications, or demonstrated site control for a new or redeveloped project underway before the new rule is finalized.

letters.desc: iMasons urges a clear transition mechanism so any new rules apply prospectively and projects with substantial sunk costs or binding equipment commitments can be grandfathered under existing processes.
quotes: iMasons supports a final rule that establishes a clear transition mechanism, and is effective on a prospective basis only, so that any existing large load projects already in development are not disrupted.

letters.org: Invenergy Wind Development North America LLCInvenergy Solar Development North America LLCInvenergy Thermal Development Holdings LLC ,
letters.desc: Invenergy asks that any transition to new interconnection rules not penalize large load customers that have already invested time and money navigating existing state processes. Transition rules should grandfather or accommodate those with prior commitments.
quotes: Invenergy urges the Commission, while it undertakes these reforms, to adopt a transition process that does not prejudice existing large load interconnection customers that have already spent time and committed resources navigating existing state interconnection processes.

letters.desc: Microsoft supports transition plans that mitigate existing risk without creating new regulatory uncertainty, covering projects under study, those already built or paid for, and facilities phasing in or operating.
quotes: Microsoft is supportive of transition plans that mitigate existing risk and do not create new regulatory risk or uncertainty for projects. A transition plan should provide regulatory stability for large loads that are already under study; large loads for which the study process has already been completed, payments made, and construction commenced; and for facilities that are phasing in or are fully operational.

letters.desc: National Grid urges a transition period shielding projects in advanced stages of development from reevaluation under new criteria, consistent with the Order No. 2023 transition approach. This avoids disrupting investments made in reliance on existing state regulatory frameworks.
quotes: Establishing a reasonable transition period is essential to ensure a smooth regulatory shift while maintaining continuity for large load interconnection projects already in advanced stages under retail interconnection procedures.

letters.desc: NRECA calls for a reasonable, orderly transition that coordinates new large-load rules with ongoing generator interconnection, transmission service, and planning processes. Regional flexibility in treating existing load interconnection studies already under way is also requested.
quotes: A reasonable, orderly and comprehensive transition period will be necessary. The proposed reforms, in whatever form, would require coordination with existing generator-interconnection, transmission-service request, and transmission-planning processes.

letters.desc: Tract supports a transition plan that gives existing interconnection applicants the option to benefit from new rules without being required to re-study or bear added costs, avoiding cascading delays.
quotes: Tract agrees that there must be a plan to implement the proposed reforms that recognize the time, capital, and effort spent on requests that are already being studied for interconnection. Negatively affecting those existing requests not only wastes individual requestor's time, capital, and effort, but could also negatively impact all large load requests by causing cascading re-studies that delay or increase the costs of other large load requests.

letters.desc: TAPS insists protections must apply to large load interconnections already under study and earlier network upgrades already governed by retail stranded-cost provisions, not only future loads covered by a new standard rule.
quotes: the Commission should ensure that other customers are protected from harm resulting from large data center load interconnections already being studied, as well as earlier data center-driven network upgrades that are subject to ratepayer protection provisions by contract or retail tariff.

letters.desc: Vistra requests that any new pro forma procedures apply prospectively only, that customers in existing study processes be allowed to continue under current rules, and that interconnection agreements filed before the final rule's effective date not be rejected for failing to conform to new procedures -- mirroring the Order No. 2003 transition approach.
quotes: the Commission should also clarify that its new pro forma procedures only apply prospectively, consistent with the rule against retroactive ratemaking.  The Commission should propose a transition process that permits customers that are interconnecting under other processes (such as the necessary study process or any applicable state-level process) to choose whether to continue through those processes or under any new procedures that the Commission adopts.
